target_customer: Engineering and quality teams at manufacturers of pressure vessels, aerospace, semiconductor, medical device and custom machinery parts
problem: Reviewing 2D mechanical drawings for GD&T, tolerance stack-ups and standards compliance takes a day or more per drawing and misses errors that scrap parts. HERA automates the review against ASME Y14.5 and ISO.
business_model: B2B software (per-seat or per-review pricing not stated)
product_category: AI engineering drawing review and engineering back-office agents

founders.name: Meera Patel
education: Industrial and Systems Engineering, University of Washington
founders.background_notes: YC page says she built a discrete-event simulation and taught herself PLC programming and C++. UW article says she began HERA by building a simulation platform.

founders.name: Noelle So
education: Industrial and Systems Engineering, University of Washington
founders.background_notes: YC page says she built a water-treatment facility at an industrial park her family runs in the Philippines.

competitors.traction_then: 2026 blog on best AI for engineering drawings

competitors.traction_then: Described by Design News as an AI tool for engineers

technical_complexity.rationale: Reading drawings and checking them against ASME Y14.5 and ISO standards with traceable findings needs domain-specific rules plus vision and LLM work. Feasible for a small team but accuracy on real drawings is the hard part.

defensibility.rationale: Several startups and vendors already ship drawing review. Switching costs could come from workflow integration, but none is shown yet.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: As of the batch no incumbent was found copying or buying HERA; outcome unknown.

market_need_then: The YC page describes reviews taking a full day or more per drawing and errors causing scrapped parts. A 2026 buyer's guide notes demand for first pass drawing checks.

branding.domain_note: The slug and original domain were manufacturingintelligence.org, which redirects (308) to heraengineering.com, indicating a rename to HERA with the domain heraengineering.com.

identity.visual_style: Imagery of drawings, CNC machining and an impeller

rebrands.why: Not stated; inferred only from the domain redirect, so treat as unverified

branding.community_and_virality: Site says users in 18 countries and offers 100 free engineering calculators as Excel files, a possible acquisition channel.

brand_strength.rationale: The name is short but shared with several unrelated Hera companies, including an Australian structural engineering firm and a video tool, which causes search confusion.

outcome_analysis: HERA is an active Summer 2026 company. Founders with factory exposure and engineering degrees picked a painful, repetitive review job, and the free calculator library may help distribution. The risks are crowded competition from CoLab and others, the need for very high accuracy on safety-relevant drawings and the small team.
notes: The $550,000 pre-seed figure comes from a UW article that names Y Combinator and no other investors; Dealroom lists a $125k seed and Seattle, an aggregator conflict. The website lists three products (Review, Autodrafting, P&ID Agent) beyond the YC page's drawing review. Outcome search found no news of a shutdown or acquisition. Founder education from the UW article; prior employers from the YC page.
